assessment: The new experiment separates ordering preferences from registered inference blocks. All ground-registry queries remain Native UNKNOWN, registry_native_admitted stays false, and usable stays empty. Seven, eleven and seven grounded instances become eligible only as context-checked primitive ordering hints. This policy does not change old skipped arms or failed runs.

The 80 successful symbolic proposal packets changed candidate ordering at 72 recorded decisions. These are trace-derived ordering counts, not measurements of realized cluster execution. On the first positive target, SC fails at 600 primitive extensions while S0 succeeds at 14. Repeated already-derived conclusions are a concrete weakness in the current preference rule.

All twelve point arms returned budget UNKNOWN, with 205 placement events and 24 exhaustive domain audits in total. The six cluster-enabled point arms recorded no successful proposal or activation. Completed empty-proposal calls can be examined passively; unlogged cutoff work remains unknown. No phase timing establishes an audit bottleneck.

The 144 returned word-reference controls and full model correspondence checks belong to resource-admitted jobs. Markings remove twelve initial candidate incidences in both paired comparisons per case. They are shallow certified first-row exclusions, not learned multiscale proof abstractions.

The first conventional recipient certificate repeats an earlier result. The three elementary donor proofs were searched anew in each cold job and used to freeze the inventory. No human proof route was supplied. No reinforcement-learning policy was trained.

The historical comparison changes the policy and number of executed point arms: two per case previously, four now. Aggregate placements and whole-job peaks therefore do not measure equivalent workloads or demonstrate speedup. Within this new cohort all six methods share the same statement, primitive grammar and declared local budgets.

Next, measure the proposal funnel explicitly and evaluate a general novelty-aware cluster preference against the unchanged primitive control. A heuristic repair must be tested in a fresh reviewed experiment; it cannot improve this frozen result retrospectively.

The program remains active: practical boundary tiling, hierarchical receptor and lemma inventories, trained proposals, automated arithmetic and symbolic Hilbert geometry, and honest conventional benchmarks. Physical universal Wang qualification and Turtle/Penrose plane constructions remain unfinished.

next_minimal_algorithmic_proposal.rationale: The rule depends on actual prefix novelty, not a target name, authored proof route or successful-case command sequence. It prevents the demonstrated repeated-conclusion attractor and gives a simple useful-proof-growth feature for a later learned ranker.

next_point_step_separate.fairness: Apply the same baseline preference to P00/P01/P10/P11; do not engineer a weak no-cluster arm or hardcode the conventional proof. This should test whether useful receptors become available, not assume they will.
next_point_step_separate.generic_direction: Give all four point arms the same simple formula-novelty tie-break among candidates at the graph-selected branch point, retaining global DEAD/FORCED/earliest-generation decisions and every original key. Rank repeated completed-prefix formulas after novel ones; hints can then order within a declared novelty tier.
